verdict: Northern Trust earned $642.9M, up 40% from a year ago, as trust fees and net interest income both grew by double digits while costs rose only 5% — though the quarter included $48.7M of one-off gains.

segments.name: Net interest income
segments.note: Interest earned on loans and securities ($2,073.1M) minus interest paid on deposits and borrowings ($1,401.7M) — up 14% from $590.8M a year ago.

segments.name: Noninterest income
segments.note: Mostly trust, investment and servicing fees of $1,373.0M (+8%) charged for safekeeping and managing client assets, plus $250.0M of other noninterest income, which included $48.7M of one-off gains (see one-time items).

opex.name: Compensation & benefits
opex.note: Pay and benefits for 23,800 employees — the bank's biggest cost, up only 3% YoY.

opex.name: Equipment & software
opex.note: Technology systems and software, including depreciation — up 9% YoY on higher technology spending.

opex.name: Outside services
opex.note: Outside providers and professional services — up 2% YoY.

opex.name: Other operating expense
opex.note: Account servicing and other day-to-day operating costs — up 25% YoY.

otherDetail: There is no separate below-the-line 'other income' step in this presentation: everything above pre-tax income sits in revenue and expenses. Pre-tax income was $796.5M, and the effective tax rate was an unusually low 19.3%.
follow100Note: Rows may add to $99.99 or $100.01 due to rounding. Northern Trust headlines revenue on a fully taxable-equivalent (FTE) basis — $2,302.1M; this page uses GAAP revenue of $2,294.4M, and net income is the same either way.

takeaways.title: Fees grew in all three businesses
takeaways.text: Trust, investment and servicing fees rose 8% to $1,373.0M, with organic fee growth in Asset Servicing, Wealth Management and Asset Management alike, helped by assets under custody/administration rising 9% to $19.9 trillion.

takeaways.title: Costs barely grew, so profit leapt
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 13% while expenses rose only 5% — strong operating leverage. Excluding notable items, management said revenue grew 11% and pre-tax income 21%. Net income rose 40% to $642.9M and return on average common equity was 20.1%.

takeaways.title: A low tax rate helped too
takeaways.text: The effective tax rate fell to 19.3% from 26.1% a year ago, mainly on a lower tax impact from international operations — part of why EPS grew 48%, faster than pre-tax income's 29%.

oneTimers: Other noninterest income included $48.7M of pre-tax notable gains: a $34.0M gain on selling the guardianship services business and a $14.7M incremental gain from Northern Trust's participation in the second Visa Exchange Offer (combined after-tax value $36.8M).
footerNote: Adaptation for a bank/trust company, following the JPMorgan page: revenue = net interest income plus noninterest income, and the $5.4M provision for credit losses plays the role of cost of revenue. Figures are GAAP; Northern Trust's headline revenue and net interest income are on a fully taxable-equivalent basis ($2,302.1M and $679.1M). Net income is total net income of $642.9M; net income applicable to common stock was $626.7M after $16.2M of preferred dividends.
